_readme: The two calibration sets of COLLECTION.md §4, PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-06 before any verdict or entry_stage was written, and before the base was built. The stage key was assembled from external documents first (one cited round announcement per row, web-verified in this run); the blind pass then judges the same rows through the production protocol with this file out of context. Scores and the layer decisions they force are in scratch/gate.md.

membership_traps._note: First Round's trap classes come from four sources: (1) the founders' PRE-FUND angel book, which the firm published on its own site under 'investments made prior to First Round Capital' (decisions.md D-T2a); (2) Howard Morgan, a co-founder whose First Round tenure ends on the 2012 fund filings and who then built a second career at Argand Partners (private equity) and B Capital — his post-2014 Form D seats are next-firm and his co-investment LPs are fund-shaped; (3) partners who arrived from operating or founding jobs (Hayley Barna/Birchbox, Elizabeth Wessel/Campus Job) or left for their own firms (Phin Barnes/General Partnership); (4) plain homonyms on common names. Expected verdicts were written from the filing dates against the roster tenure windows in sources/roster-curated.json, before the grind. TRUE rows are mixed in across eras so the set measures precision, not suspicion.

membership_traps.gate: Zero false members at high confidence before any verdict writes.
membership_traps._slug_correction: 2026-09-06, before the blind pass: five trap slugs were rewritten to the slugs the build actually produced (apptronik->apptronik-inc, precision-neuroscience->precision-neuroscience-corp, kentik-technologies->kentik, campus-job->campus-job-inc, posit-science->posit-science-corp). Expected verdicts were not touched. `in_base` records, per row, whether the row reached the base at all: 17 of the 23 traps were removed by the build's own structural filters (fund-shaped LPs, personal Section 16 filings, ex-partner tenure, non-portfolio industry) or never entered because the pre-fund page is deliberately not a configured listing surface — those are passes scored before the judge, and the six that survive are what the blind pass has to rule on.

stage_golden._note: 18 rows, each anchored to one external round announcement, spanning 2006-2019 and all three of the firm's own label values. The set is deliberately weighted toward rows where the firm's own `initialPartnership` field (live Sanity CMS, 195 rows) and its archived twin (the 2020-2024 WordPress accordion, 302 rows) can be SCORED — that field is the candidate class-1 layer for this investor, and §4 requires it to be measured before the grind may treat it as a label. It is short of §4's 30-40 because the web-search budget is a run constraint (§8 lesson 4) and this base is large enough that the A/B pass and the momentum slice need the remainder; every row here is anchored, none is padded.

rows.note: The firm now labels this Pre-Seed; the 2006 record calls it a seed round, and §6 says the label follows what the firm AND the record call the round.
The $800k seed (Sept 2012) was angels and Graph Ventures; First Round and Bessemer entered at the February 2013 Series A.
Roblox's own 2005 Series A predates First Round; the firm entered at the 2009 round the record calls a seed, alongside Altos. A deliberate hard case: chronologically post-A, named Seed.
$68M with no named series; §6 bands anything at Series-B scale and later as Growth. The firm's own label says Series A.

stage_golden.gate: The set is measured blind through the production protocol before entry_stage publishes; misses are decomposed by layer, and the layer is fixed, never the instance. The firm's own initialPartnership field is scored here and promoted or demoted by that score.
